channel.title: Trend Reader
channel.description: The AI vocabulary, mapped: a weekly brief on the terms and themes to know, and every new term as it is defined.

item.title: Weekly brief, week W43: Decision model, Calibration
item.description: This week's terms: Decision model, Calibration. concept · Models & architectures

item.title: New term: Approval fatigue
item.description: Approval fatigue is the degradation of human-in-the-loop oversight that follows from asking a person to approve too many agent actions, which pushes users to grant broad standing permissions instead. It matters because the remedies for it, not the interception mechanism, are where agent permission systems actually fail.

item.title: New term: Calibration
item.description: Calibration is the agreement between a model's stated confidence and the long-run frequency with which predictions at that confidence turn out correct. It matters because any system that acts on a model's confidence — routing, abstaining, escalating — is only as sound as that number.

item.title: New term: Decision model
item.description: A decision model is a model that returns a choice from a fixed set of options together with calibrated probabilities, rather than generating text. It matters because the routing, guardrail and verification decisions inside AI systems are single-bit questions that a generative model answers slowly and expensively.

item.title: New term: MATCH Act
item.description: The MATCH Act is United States legislation that would raise export controls on the most capable semiconductor manufacturing equipment, including deep ultraviolet immersion lithography, from entity-based restrictions to countrywide ones. It matters because lithography tools are the chokepoint where export control retains the most leverage over how much AI compute can physically be built.

item.title: New term: Maia 300
item.description: Maia 300 is Microsoft's third-generation custom inference accelerator, announced for 2027 data centres with a company-reported 40 percent more tokens per watt than leading GPU-based systems. It matters because it commits the largest reseller of other companies' compute to serving its own products on its own silicon.

item.title: New term: Muse Wonder
item.description: Muse Wonder is Meta's first frontier model family, released in October 2026 and claimed comparable to the leading models from OpenAI and Anthropic, with an emphasis on retaining personal information over time. It matters because it made Meta a frontier competitor roughly a year after the company was widely written off.

item.title: New term: Scion
item.description: Scion is an internal version-control system built to replace Git at a merge rate conventional tooling could not sustain. It matters because it is the first widely reported case of agent-written code breaking a standard engineering tool rather than a standard engineering practice.
